chapter_name: Yoga and its Relevance in the Modern Times
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the ancient origins of Yoga, Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga (Eight Limbs), and how Asanas and Pranayama relieve modern stress and posture issues!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derived from the Sanskrit root 'Yuj' meaning to join or unite. It is a harmonious discipline connecting individual consciousness with universal consciousness, integrating body, mind, and spirit.

The Eight Limbs of Yoga: 1) Yama (social ethics), 2) Niyama (personal discipline), 3) Asana (postures), 4) Pranayama (breath control), 5) Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), 6) Dharana (concentration), 7) Dhyana (meditation), 8) Samadhi (enlightenment).
Practicing standing, sitting, and lying asanas (like Tadasana, Bhujangasana, and Vajrasana) corrects spinal posture, increases flexibility, and prevents lifestyle ailments.
Controlled breathing exercises (such as Anulom-Vilom and Bhramari) balance the nervous system, lower anxiety, improve lung capacity, and enhance focus.

fun_activity.title: 🫁 Bhramari (Bee Breath) Relaxation
fun_activity.instructions: Sit comfortably with your back straight. Close your eyes, plug your ears gently with your index fingers, inhale deeply through your nose, and exhale slowly while humming like a bee ('Mmmmm'). Feel the vibrations calm your mind!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the names and correct sequence of Patanjali's Eight Limbs (Ashtanga Yoga) without altering the order.
📌 Know which specific asana is recommended for which lifestyle issue (e.g., Vajrasana for digestion after meals, Tadasana for height and posture).
📌 Differentiate between Yama (external social discipline like Ahimsa, Satya) and Niyama (internal personal observance like Shaucha, Santosha).
quick_recap: ⭐ International Day of Yoga is celebrated worldwide every year on June 21st.
⭐ Vajrasana is unique because it is the only yogic posture that can be safely practiced immediately after eating food.
⭐ Regular practice of Pranayama calms mental turbulence and improves concentration.
